title: Relative tensor and K-flatness under the internal-to-sectionwise module equivalence
statement:
Let $C$ be a site whose objects and morphisms lie in the coefficient universe. Assume abelian sheafification exists, its local equivalences are monoidal, and the category $\mathcal A=\operatorname{Sh}(C,\operatorname{Ab})$ has the closed symmetric monoidal structure given by sheafified objectwise tensor over $\mathbf Z$ [det-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor-structure, sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor]. Let $R$ be a commutative ring object of $\mathcal A$, let $R_{\mathrm{sec}}$ be its reconstructed section-ring sheaf, and let
$$E_R:\operatorname{Mod}_R(\mathcal A)\simeq\operatorname{Mod}(R_{\mathrm{sec}})$$
be the equivalence of [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence], which leaves underlying abelian sheaves and maps unchanged. Give the source the coequalizer relative tensor [def-sfb-modobj-relative-tensor] and the target the sheafification of sectionwise balanced tensor [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Then $E_R$ is exact and has natural isomorphisms
$$E_R(M\otimes_RN)\cong E_R(M)\otimes_{R_{\mathrm{sec}}}E_R(N),\qquad E_R(R)\cong R_{\mathrm{sec}},$$
characterized on local pure tensors by $m\otimes n\mapsto m\otimes n$. These comparisons respect associators, unitors and symmetry. Applied termwise to cochain complexes [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], $E_R$ identifies the direct-sum total tensor complexes [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves] and preserves and reflects acyclicity, flat modules [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules] and K-flat complexes [def-pc-kflat-complex]; in the internal category, flatness and K-flatness mean the same exact-tensor and acyclic-total-tensor tests.

source.place: Tag 03EK, section-tensor-product, balanced-bilinear universal property; Tag 0GMW, lemma-sheafification-tensor. Internal-module comparison and passage to total complexes are the extracted agent argument.

proof.text: The equivalence in [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence] is obtained by evaluating the internal multiplication and action on sections and reconstructing the section-ring sheaf; its forward functor preserves the underlying abelian sheaves, section groups, restriction maps, and morphisms identically. The sheaf tensor and its local pure tensors are the sheafified objectwise tensors of [det-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor-structure]. Thus for every internal module the object, every map, and every local pure tensor have the displayed sectionwise interpretation under $E_R$.

source.place: Tag 00YV, algebraic structures in a ringed topos; literature/stacks-project/sites-modules.tex, section-tensor-product

proof.text: By [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor], tensor on abelian sheaves preserves colimits in either variable and is additive; in particular $R\otimes-$ preserves finite colimits. Thus [lem-sfb-modobj-abelian] applies, and the source is abelian. Its forgetful functor preserves finite limits and finite colimits by [lem-sfb-modobj-forget-left-exact] and [lem-sfb-modobj-forget-right-exact]. The target is abelian with sectionwise kernels and sheafified sectionwise cokernels by [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and its forgetful functor is faithful and exact by [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful]. Both underlying sheaf functors therefore compute kernels and cokernels. The sectionwise equivalence of step 1 preserves addition on morphisms and identifies these sheaves and their induced actions. Hence it preserves and reflects kernels, cokernels and exact sequences: $E_R$ is an exact additive equivalence.

source.place: Tags 03DA and 03DB, abelian module sheaves and exact forgetful functor; literature/blueprint/main-20261015/blueprint/sec-proetale-coefficients/sk-prop-sfb-module-category/sk-prop-sfb-module-category.proof.md, Part 1

proof.text: The relative tensor in [def-sfb-modobj-relative-tensor] is the coequalizer $M\otimes R\otimes N\rightrightarrows M\otimes N$, with the action through $M$. A map from it to an internal module $P$ is therefore a map from $M\otimes N$ to $P$ satisfying $b(rm,n)=b(m,rn)$, and linear for the action on the first factor. By [det-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor-structure] and the universal property of sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification], maps out of the sheaf tensor correspond to restriction-compatible sectionwise biadditive maps. The two conditions just displayed say exactly that $b$ is sectionwise $R_{\mathrm{sec}}$-bilinear. Conversely any such bilinear map has these properties, so factors uniquely through the coequalizer. A map from the sheafification of $U\mapsto M(U)\otimes_{R_{\mathrm{sec}}(U)}N(U)$ to $E_RP$ likewise corresponds, by [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] and the universal property of module sheafification [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] (whose underlying abelian sheaf is the abelian sheafification), to precisely these compatible bilinear maps. The universal maps in each direction are mutually inverse because their composites fix $m\otimes n$; uniqueness follows from the same universal properties. This gives the natural comparison, with pure tensors sent to identically named pure tensors. These constructions use abelian sheaves and their sheafification, rather than requiring a section functor to preserve cokernels.

source.place: Tag 03EK, section-tensor-product, balanced-bilinear universal property; Tag 0GMW, lemma-sheafification-tensor

proof.text: The regular module $R$ is sent to $R_{\mathrm{sec}}$ by the action construction in [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence], giving the unit comparison. The source associator and unitors are induced from those before the coequalizer [def-sfb-modobj-relative-tensor]; its symmetry descends from the ambient braiding [def-sfb-modobj-symmetric-tensor]. The target structures are the sectionwise ones of [lem-pc-sheaf-modules-tensor-closed]. On local pure tensors the associativity comparison sends $(m\otimes n)\otimes p$ to $m\otimes(n\otimes p)$ on both sides, symmetry sends $m\otimes n$ to $n\otimes m$, and the unitors send $r\otimes m$ and $m\otimes r$ to $rm$. Equality on these tensors implies equality of the sheaf maps by the sheafification and coequalizer universal properties used in step 3. Thus all comparison diagrams for associators, unitors and symmetry commute.

source.place: Tag 03EK, associativity and symmetry of the section tensor; Tag 00YV, regular module

proof.text: Apply $E_R$ degreewise to cochain complexes; it preserves addition and composition, hence the differential equations. The target has all small direct sums by [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful]. If $G$ is a quasi-inverse of $E_R$, a coproduct $S=\bigoplus_i E_R M_i$ supplies a source coproduct $GS$: the bijections $\operatorname{Hom}(GS,P)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(S,E_RP)\cong\prod_i\operatorname{Hom}(E_RM_i,E_RP)\cong\prod_i\operatorname{Hom}(M_i,P)$ identify its universal maps. Thus $E_R$ identifies these direct sums. For each degree $n$, apply this with the countable index $p+q=n$ and the tensor comparisons of step 3. Naturality of those comparisons in each differential, and additivity of $E_R$, make the resulting degreewise isomorphisms commute with $d_M\otimes1+(-1)^p1\otimes d_N$, including its sign. By [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves] this is exactly the direct-sum total tensor differential. Hence the degreewise isomorphisms form a natural isomorphism of total complexes.

Because $E_R$ is exact and additive, kernels, images, and cokernels of every differential are carried to the corresponding target objects. The cohomology definition in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] therefore gives natural isomorphisms $H^n(E_RK)\cong E_R(H^nK)$. An equivalence reflects the zero object, so a complex is acyclic in the internal category exactly when its image is acyclic in the section-module category.

For a module $F$, flatness in the internal category means that $-\otimes_RF$ is exact, while flatness in the section category means that $-\otimes_{R_{\mathrm{sec}}}E_R(F)$ is exact, as in [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. The natural tensor isomorphism of step 3 identifies these two functors after applying the exact equivalence $E_R$. Since $E_R$ preserves and reflects exact sequences by step 2, one functor is exact if and only if the other is. This proves preservation and reflection of flat modules.

Let $K$ be an internal cochain complex. For every acyclic internal complex $A$, step 5 gives a natural isomorphism between $E_R(\operatorname{Tot}(A\otimes_RK))$ and $\operatorname{Tot}(E_RA\otimes_{R_{\mathrm{sec}}}E_RK)$. Step 6 says that $A$ is acyclic exactly when $E_RA$ is acyclic, and the same step says that total-complex acyclicity is preserved and reflected. Consequently the defining test in [def-pc-kflat-complex] holds for $K$ exactly when it holds for $E_RK$. Hence $E_R$ preserves and reflects K-flat complexes; the assertion about internal flatness and K-flatness is precisely the two defining exact-tensor and acyclic-total-tensor tests. To check that the forward implication tests every target acyclic complex $B$, apply the quasi-inverse $G$ termwise to $B$ and its differentials. The counit gives a chain isomorphism $E_R(GB)\cong B$; step 6 makes $GB$ acyclic. Step 5 then identifies the tested target tensor with the image of the corresponding source tensor. For the reverse implication, test directly on $E_RA$ for each acyclic source complex $A$ and reflect its tensor's acyclicity using step 6.
